1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early days of the forecast horizon — adjust initial forecast values downward by 1–3% for short-term (1–7 day) horizons.

2. After sharp price spikes (e.g., >30% from prior day), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — reduce forecast by 5–10% in the 2–5 day window following the spike.

3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if 30-day history shows strong upward trend, forecast should not exceed 1.5x the 30-day average unless confirmed by strong macro signals.

4. Forecast lags behind true price movements by 2–5 days — apply a 1–2 day lag correction for 10–30 day horizons, especially when true price moves >5% in 1–3 days.

5. Model overreacts to recent volatility — if 7-day moving average of true prices is rising, reduce forecast slope to match slower trend; avoid exponential growth in forecast after volatility spikes.

6. For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period corrections — add a 1–2 day downward adjustment if true price shows a sharp decline in last 5–7 days of history.
